issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency: the problem statement asks students to implement a function named _construct_zero_state_prep_circuit (with a leading underscore), whereas both the template repository and the solution repository define the function as construct_zero_state_prep_circuit (no leading underscore). This mismatch can confuse students about which symbol to implement and will cause automated tests or graders that expect the name in code to fail to find the implemented function.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: update the problem statement to request construct_zero_state_prep_circuit (no leading underscore) to match the template and solution. Alternatively, rename the function in the template and solution to _construct_zero_state_prep_circuit so all three artifacts use the same identifier.

issues.description: The problem statement names the state-preparation function with a leading underscore, while the template and solution define the same conceptual function without the underscore. Concept: a function that constructs a Stim circuit preparing the logical |0> state from the X-check matrix. Problem statement identifier: `_construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(Hx: npt.NDArray[np.int8], offset: int=0) -> stim.Circuit`. Template identifier: `construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(Hx: npt.NDArray[np.int8], offset:int=0) -> stim.Circuit` (defined in template_repository/msd.py). Solution identifier: `construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(...)` (defined in solution_repository/msd.py). This mismatch can confuse students about which function to implement and may lead to misnamed implementations vs. test expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Prefer changing the problem statement to reference `construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(Hx: npt.NDArray[np.int8], offset: int=0) -> stim.Circuit` (remove leading underscore) so it matches the template and solution. Alternatively, rename the template and solution functions to `_construct_zero_state_prep_circuit`, but keeping the public name without a leading underscore is recommended.
